weather.tip: 99% rain chance today — carry an umbrella and rain cover for your commute, and build in extra buffer time given the Muharram procession and VIP-related traffic diversions already in place.

around.headline: Muharram procession brings traffic diversions today
around.summary: Police have announced traffic diversions across Bengaluru, including on Hosur Road, for today's Muharram procession. If your commute crosses these stretches, plan an alternate route or extra time.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Traffic curbs continue around Lok Bhavan for new ministers' induction
around.summary: Restrictions are in place near Lok Bhavan as Karnataka's newly inducted ministers are sworn in. Avoid the CBD stretch around Vidhana Soudha/Lok Bhavan if possible today.

around.headline: Bengaluru–Mangaluru rail link back after landslide
around.summary: Train services on the Bengaluru–Mangaluru route resumed August 3 after a two-day hiatus caused by a landslide on the track near Sakleshpur. If you're travelling this route, check PNR/running status before heading out.

around.headline: Cybercrook duped an 82-year-old of Rs 3 lakh using a fake voter-list (SIR) call
around.summary: A conman used the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls as a pretext to swindle an elderly Bengaluru resident of Rs 3 lakh. Genuine SIR checks are done in person by a BLO with an ID card — never by phone or OTP.

around.headline: Delivery executive assaulted and robbed of scooter
around.summary: A food/parcel delivery worker was assaulted and had his scooter robbed while on duty in the city. If you see a delivery worker in distress, calling 112 immediately can help before the situation escalates.

around.headline: Gandhinagar gets Bengaluru's first integrated fire hydrant network
around.summary: The white-topped roads in Gandhinagar now come with an integrated fire hydrant system, part of a wider plan to revive the city's long-dormant hydrant network, including on Pete-area roads. It's a small but real upgrade to how fast fire response can be in these localities.

around.headline: Lok Sabha passes bill to expand Supreme Court to 38 judges
around.summary: Parliament's lower house passed a bill raising the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength, including the CJI, from 34 to 38 judges. More judges could mean faster disposal of the court's long-pending case backlog over time.

events.name: Kunal Kamra stand-up show — moved to Koramangala
events.note: The comedian relocated his Bengaluru shows from Whitefield to a Koramangala venue after a right-wing outfit objected. Check the ticket platform for the updated venue before you head out.

events.name: Feast of Flavours
events.note: A food-focused city event — a good pick if you want to sample a wide spread of cuisines in one stop.

events.name: Art transforms into tool for environment protection
events.note: An art exhibition/initiative in the city framing art as a tool for environmental awareness — worth a look if you're into art with a civic angle.

street_smart.title: A caller says he's verifying your details for the SIR (voter list revision) and needs an OTP right now to 'confirm' your registration.
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India Bengaluru: a cybercrook used the SIR (Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls) as bait to defraud an 82-year-old resident of Rs 3 lakh. This is a fresh angle on SIR-related fraud — a phone/OTP scam — distinct from the door-to-door BLO impersonation scenario used on 2026-07-30, so it's not a repeat within the 3-week window.
street_smart.situation: Your phone rings and the caller says they're calling about the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of voter rolls — your name may be removed unless you 'verify' right now. They ask you to confirm by reading out the OTP that's about to land on your phone. What do you do?

choices.text: Read out the OTP since it's about your voter registration and the caller sounds official.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. An OTP is the key that authorizes a bank transaction, UPI payment, or account login — voter-roll verification never needs one. The moment you read it out, the scammer uses it to approve a transfer from your account or a linked service, not to 'confirm' your voter status.

choices.text: Refuse the OTP, but read out your Aadhaar number and date of birth to 'prove' who you are instead.
choices.feedback: Also a trap. These details combine with whatever the scammer already has (your phone number, maybe a leaked database entry) to impersonate you elsewhere — for SIM swaps, loan apps, or KYC fraud. No genuine SIR call needs you to recite ID numbers over the phone either.

choices.text: Hang up, then independently verify by calling your ward's BBMP helpline or visiting the local BLO/Election office using a number you look up yourself.
choices.feedback: Correct. Real SIR verification is done in person by a designated Booth Level Officer carrying an ID card — it is never conducted by an unsolicited phone call, and never involves an OTP or payment. Verifying independently, through a number you find yourself, defeats a spoofed caller ID or manufactured urgency.

choices.text: Stay on the line and ask the caller to send a written notice by post, then wait for it before doing anything.
choices.feedback: Risky. It's safer than sharing information, but staying passive leaves you open to a fake follow-up email or link. Better to hang up, verify proactively through official channels, and report the call to the cyber-crime helpline right away.

takeaways: SIR/voter-roll checks are done in person by a BLO with a visible ID card — never by phone, OTP, or payment.
Never read out an OTP to anyone who calls you, no matter what reason they give — it is the key to your money, not to your identity.
Report suspicious calls to India's cyber-crime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in as soon as they happen, even if you didn't lose money — it helps flag the number for others.

quiz.question: What caused a two-day disruption to Bengaluru–Mangaluru train services this week, before service resumed on August 3?
quiz.why: The Western Ghats' steep, rain-soaked slopes make landslides a recurring monsoon hazard for rail lines through districts like Hassan and Dakshina Kannada.

quiz.question: Which Bengaluru locality just got the city's first integrated fire hydrant network under its white-topped roads?
quiz.why: Integrating hydrants into white-topped road projects lets civic agencies lay the underground piping once, alongside road works, instead of digging up finished roads later.

quiz.question: The Lok Sabha this week passed a bill raising the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength (including the CJI) from 34 to how many judges?
quiz.why: The Supreme Court's original 1950 sanctioned strength was just 8 judges; Parliament has expanded it several times since as case pendency grew.

quiz.question: Which river supplies most of Bengaluru's drinking water, pumped in from roughly 100 km away?
quiz.why: Unlike most major Indian cities, Bengaluru isn't built on a riverbank — it relies on water lifted from the Cauvery through a multi-stage pumping system, which is also why supply is so sensitive to power costs and monsoon flow.

quiz.question: What does the 'P' in UPI (India's instant payment system) stand for?
quiz.why: UPI — Unified Payments Interface — is built and operated by NPCI; its instant, OTP/PIN-based design is exactly why scammers try to trick users into sharing OTPs, rather than needing your card or bank password.
